TRRAINHer Ascent – Livelihood program, aims at training and creating livelihood opportunities for women in retail. It focuses on providing employment to those who want to join the retail industry. This is a carefully designed skills training program that primarily focuses on retail skills and life skills. Through this livelihood program, TRRAIN aims to promote a gender diverse workforce in retail. TRRAIN Pankh District Raipur Mysore Warangal Chitradurga Tumkur Krishna Dharwad Bangalore Rural Chandigarh Hyderabad Kolkata Bellary Davangere Kamrup Cuddapah Kolar Chittoor Bagalkot Thane Jaipur Pune Bhopal Khordha Indore Vadodara Ahmedabad Gautam Buddha Nagar Rajkot Surat Gandhinagar Dehradun Lucknow Agra Salem Sri Sathya Sai Allahabad Coimbatore Ranchi Mumbai Chennai North Kannada Visakhapatnam Gurgaon Kottayam Nandyal Tirupati State Andhra Pradesh Karnataka Odisha Tamil Nadu West Bengal Chhattisgarh Assam Chandigarh Delhi Gujarat Jharkhand Madhya Pradesh Maharashtra Uttar Pradesh Uttarakhand Telangana District Raipur Mysore Warangal Chitradurga Tumkur Krishna Dharwad Bangalore Rural Chandigarh Hyderabad Kolkata Bellary Davangere Kamrup Cuddapah Kolar Chittoor Bagalkot Thane Jaipur Pune Bhopal Khordha Indore Vadodara Ahmedabad Gautam Buddha Nagar Rajkot Surat Gandhinagar Dehradun Lucknow Agra Salem Sri Sathya Sai Allahabad Coimbatore Ranchi Mumbai Chennai North Kannada Visakhapatnam Gurgaon Kottayam Nandyal Tirupati States Andhra Pradesh Karnataka Odisha Tamil Nadu West Bengal Chhattisgarh Assam Chandigarh Delhi Gujarat Jharkhand Madhya Pradesh Maharashtra Uttar Pradesh Uttarakhand Telangana According to the 2011 census, there are approximately 2.7 Crore Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) in India and the heart-wrenching truth is that their employability is less than 1%. There are many reasons for this extremely low number. Through the TRRAIN Pankh program we aim to tackle 3 barriers that are responsible for this situation: 1. Lack of skilling/training of PwDs. 2. Lack of employment opportunities for PwDs. 3. The importance of their inclusion in the retail and allied industries. Launched in 2011, TRRAIN’s Pankh program works towards creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) by training and providing them with employment opportunities in retail and allied sectors, thereby also promoting diversity and inclusion in the industry.
